tossups.text: On January 1, 1969, this non-American city was the start-point of a 73-mile long civil rights march, and in August of the same year, it saw widespread rioting and the conviction of Bernadette Devlin. William Whitelaw initiated a military intervention called Operation Motorman in response to violence in this city. A major politician in this city was the founder of the Martyrs Memorial Free Presbyterian Church, Ian Paisley, whose Democratic Unionist party brought him to power. This city was also the location of the signing of an April 10, 1998 agreement which established joint rule of the country where this city is the capital. The namesake alternate name of of the Good Friday Accords, for 10 points, identify this capital of Northern Ireland.

This character's sister, whose agent is nicknamed Uncle Puffs, is a singer who is nicknamed The Brass Monkey. This character's biological parents are William Methwold and Vanita, Wee Willie Winkie's wife, although he is switched with another infant at birth by the midwife Mary Pereira. He organizes a conference including such characters as his nemesis Shiva and Parvati-the-Witch, although he later loses his telepathic powers due to an operation on his enormous nose. Along with one thousand other children, he was born on August 15, 1947, in the first hour of India's independence. For 10 points, name this protagonist of Salman Rushdie's Midnight's Children.

The death of Bogislaw XIV during this war resulted in one belligerent annexing his state under the Treaty of Stettin. The War of the Mantuan Succession was a part of this larger conflict which featured the brutal sack of Magdeburg. The Treaty of Lübeck ended Christian IV's involvement with one side in this war. Count Tilly won the battle of White Mountain during this war's Bohemian phase, which began after Ferdinand II's representatives were thrown out of a window in the Second Defenestration of Prague. For 10 points, what large European war between Catholic and Protestant forces was ended by the Peace of Westphalia after three decades of fighting?

In one work by this author, the title character falls in love with Yelena Serebryakov. In addition to Uncle Vanya, he wrote a play in which Nina marries Trigorin and Konstantin Treplyov commits suicide after shooting the title bird. In another of his plays, Varya hurls a pair of keys to the floor after Lopakhin maliciously buys Madame Ranevsky's estate. For 10 points, name this playwright of The Seagull and The Cherry Orchard.

This concept is the first in the title of a book that argues that it contradicts itself because "whatever can be common always has little value." A 1903 book argues that this concept is a "simple notion" like the color yellow and compares defining it to the difficulty in defining the sensation of red. In that book, structured around three questions like "what is this concept as a means?", G. E. Moore argues that attempts to define it with related properties are fallacious. This is the first of two concepts in the title of a book that argues Christianity had created a "slave morality" with simplistic opposites; many arguments in that book are continued in On the Genealogy of Morals. For 10 points, name this quality that desirable and ethical actions should have, the first of two concepts Nietzsche sought to go beyond.

Richard Lovat Somers narrates one book set in this country and written by D. H. Lawrence. The Man Who Loved Children is by an author from this country, Christina Stead. One novel set in this country focuses on transporting a glass church, while another is about a German explorer named Voss. In addition to being the home of Banjo Paterson and the setting of Oscar and Lucinda, this country inspired the bush ballad "Waltzing Matilda." An author from this country wrote about a German saving 1,200 Jews from concentration camps. The home of Patrick White, Peter Carey, and Thomas Keneally, for 10 points, identify this country where outback literature is set.

This musician sang the lines, "They say I look like God. Could God be black?" in a jazz musical he worked on with Dave Brubeck called The Real Ambassadors. This musician collaborated on songs like "My Heart" with his second wife, Lil Hardin. With Earl Hines, this musician made recordings of "Weather Bird" and "West End Blues," both of which were written by his mentor, Joe "King" Oliver. With his "Hot Five," this musician recorded "Heebie Jeebies," which features his scat singing. For 10 points, name this jazz trumpeter nicknamed "Satchmo" who raspily sang, "I see trees of green, red roses too," in "What a Wonderful World."

The murder of this man's friend Abraham Gonzalez deepened his hatred of Victoriano Huerta. This man gained control of the vast mineral wealth of Chihuahua during his time as caudillo of that province. This man commanded the Division of the North, with which he helped the Carranza government take power before launching a raid on Columbus, New Mexico in 1916. For 10 points, name this famous Mexican revolutionary who was chased by John J. Pershing's Punitive Expedition.

These mythical figures turned the Pierides[pee-AY-rih-deez]into magpies after defeating them in a contest. These figures were the children of Mnemosyne[m'nih-MAH-sih-nee],a Titan who governed memory. In some myths, one of these figures was the mother of Orpheus, the bard. This group included Clio andCalliope, who governed history and epic poetry. For ten points, name this set of nine goddesses of creative activities like literature and dancing.

Most of John Tyler's cabinet resigned because of Tyler's opposition to Henry Clay's plan for reorganizing this. It was stabilized when William Jones was replaced by Langton Cleves, after the corruption of James Buchanan and the embezzler James McCulloch had jeopardized it. After dissolving, it became a private corporation chartered in Pennsylvania, but went insolvent five years later. Its evisceration in 1836 was symbolic of the anti-centralization ideologies and partly due to personal emnity for Nicholas Biddle. For 10 points, name this institution destroyed by Andrew Jackson.
tossups.answer: Second Bank of the United States
acceptableAnswers: Second Bank of the United States
The Second Bank of the United States

tossups.text: In one portion of this event, a man is given the hide of an African lion whose claws have been gilded with gold. Before this event begins, a character pours two bowls of wine, two bowls of fresh milk, and two bowls of hallowed blood and scatters crimson petals, which causes a huge shining snake to auspiciously appear from an altar. Gyas angrily throws Menoetes into the sea during a part of this event that also sees Sergestus run aground. During one part of this event, a man is given a Thracian mixing bowl when he shoots an arrow and it blazes like a shooting star. A man named Entellus wins a bull and then dashes its brains out with a single blow during this event. Nisus slips on some blood and manure during a foot race in this event, which occurs in the realm of King Acestes. For 10 points, name this event described in Book V of the Aeneid, in which Aeneas honors the death of his father with a variety of athletic contests.
acceptableAnswers: "Book V of the Aeneid" until it is read

tossups.text: This figure recounts seeing a blue lizard crawl up a blasphemous preacher's pants in a story collection titled for his "yarns." Bram Stoker financed multiple life masks and busts of this figure after meeting with Walt Whitman. Alexander McClure and Horatio Alger collected myths about this figure. William Mumler used double exposure to capture images of this figure standing behind a seated woman. John Locke Scripps popularized depictions of this figure carrying railfences and an axe. A nickname for this figure arose from his habit of walking dozens of miles to return shortchanged cash while working in New Haven, Illinois. This figure's ghost supposedly haunts the Yellow Oval Room in a hat whose size was likely exaggerated by this figure's height. For 10 points, name this figure mythologized as "Honest Abe."

At this site, August Mau delineated four styles of wall painting including the "incrustation" and "intricate" types. This is the larger of two sites from which objects are kept at a nearby city's "Secret Museum". Many amphorae in this location bore the name of "Scaurus", a noted manufacturer of garum. An artwork depicting the Battle of Issus is found in this city's House of the Faun, and is known as the Alexander mosaic. In this city's House of the Tragic Poet, the text "cavē canem" ("KA-weh KAN-em") appears beneath a black dog in a floor mosaic. Many erotic artworks and graffiti were uncovered during this city's excavation along with nearby Herculaneum. For 10 points, name this Roman city buried under a layer of ash in the 79 AD eruption of Mount Vesuvius.

The narrators of this poem describe themselves as "people on the pavement," and in the final stanza they note how "on we worked, and waited for the light / and went without the meat, and cursed the bread." This poem's title character is described as "quietly arrayed" and someone who "fluttered pulses when he said 'Good-morning'." That man was "imperially slim" and "admirably schooled in every grace," but on "one calm summer night" he "went home and put a bullet through his head." For 10 points, name this poem, about a "gentleman from sole to crown," written by Edwin Arlington Robinson.

This god rescued Thyone from the underworld and took her to Mount Olympus. This god's followers were the maenads,who embodied this god's dominion over frenzied, divine inspiration. This god married Ariadne after Theseus abandoned her. Zeus unintentionally killed this god's mortal mother, Semele, by appearing to her in his full glory, and then sewed this god into his thigh, making him "twice born." For ten points, name this Greek god of wine.

One artist from this country painted the huge March of Humanity artwork in the Polyforum building in this country's capital city. It's not the USA, but a work by an artist from this country was rejected by Nelson Rockefeller for depicting Vladimir Lenin, and was recreated elsewhere as Man, Controller of the Universe. In addition to those two muralists, an artist from this country included features such as hummingbirds, monkeys and this nation's border with the USA in her series of self-portraits. For 10 points, name this country home to Diego Rivera and Frida Kahlo.

This literary character stores a sixpenny birthday gift in a wooden box and eats it over several weeks. This boy receives an inheritance by outlasting a girl who falls down a trash chute and one who chews an entire meal in a stick of gum and becomes a blueberry. For 10 points, Veruca Salt and Violet Beauregard compete with what fictional boy who, in a book by Roald Dahl, tours Willy Wonka's chocolate factory?

Residents of this place remember the order of streets with the mnemonic "Jesus Christ Made [this city] Under Protest". Kris Kime was murdered during this city's 2001 Mardi Gras Riots in Pioneer Square. The multi-site Mars Hill megachurch in this city disbanded after controversies involving its pastor Mark Driscoll. This city's alternative newspaper The Stranger was the first to run an advice column by Dan Savage. Near Elliott Bay, one can find this city's Pike Place Market. A famous landmark of this city houses SkyCity, a rotating restaurant 500 feet above ground. Frank Gehry designed this King County city's Experience Music Project, which houses musical paraphernalia from Jimi Hendrix and Nirvana. For 10 points, name this West Coast city home to the Space Needle.

This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for portal systems. It plays a key role in the cardiovascular system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this systole-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The systole is a key component of the Cardiovascular system, involved in portal systems.

tossups.text: Temperature dependent sex determination in this group of animals follows pattern 1, where colder temperatures cause males and warmer temperatures cause females. Inhibiting expression of the KDM6B demethylase modifier can cause male-to-female sex reversal in some species of this animal. These animals in order testudines are among the oldest groups of reptiles, with members dating back to the middle Jurassic. Some members of this group can breathe through their cloaca by taking in water. Regardless of size, all members of this group have thirteen keratinous scutes. For 10 points, name this group of reptiles covered in a hard shell.

parts.text: Name this Spanish-language American broadcasting company and competitor of Telemundo.
Salinas has co-anchored the nightly Noticiero Univision program with this anchor since 1988. This anchor is often nicknamed the "Walter Cronkite of Latin America."
Description acceptable. Univision won a Peabody Award for its documentary exposing this US government policy, whose failure led Congress to hold Attorney General Eric Holder in contempt.
acceptableAnswers: letting guns walk across the US-Mexico border

bonuses.leadin: María Elena Salinas worked for this company's KMEX-DT affiliate in the 1980s, which was earlier led by Ruben Salazar until his death while covering the anti-Vietnam War Chicano Moratorium. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this object. While on this object, a character repeats, "I know we can fetch it," before suddenly having a vision of his wife's face.
A sled is found by the title character of this novel by Edith Wharton. At the end of this novel, Mattie Silver is paralyzed while riding the sled during a "smash-up".
The sled used in the "smash-up" is thought to belong to this character. This character's wife speaks to the narrator in the frame story of Ethan Frome.

bonuses.leadin: This object is guided toward an elm tree while a sorrel is heard whinnying. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this region of a certain east African country, which has been in near constant warfare since 2003 due to Janjaweed militants.
Darfur is a region in this large African country which is led by Omar al-Bashir from Khartoum.
A January 2011 referendum decided that the southern part of Sudan would split off and become a new country with its capital at this city on the White Nile.

bonuses.leadin: Groups based in this region include the Justice and Equality Movement and the Liberation and Justice Movement. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this author, who wrote of Natty Bumpo's first kill in his story "The Deerslayer," one of his works featured in The Leatherstocking Tales.
In this Cooper novel set in Fort William Henry, Natty Bumpo kills Magua after Cora dies in a Delaware camp.
At the end of this other Cooper work, Oliver Edwards chooses to marry Elizabeth Temple as Natty walks into the sunset.

bonuses.leadin: Mark Twain said that this author committed 114 literary offenses. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these constructs that are materially identical to humans, but do not have mental properties.
Physical zombies are used to refute the theories of this concept in philosophy of mind. Philosophers often define this concept as awareness of external and internal phenomena.

This philosopher's book Consciousness Explained presents a functionalist refutation of the existence of zombies. He also wrote about the effects of Charles Darwin's thought in Darwin's Dangerous Idea.

bonuses.leadin: David Chalmers used these constructs to argue that sentience is a further fact, meaning that it cannot be inferred from logical analysis. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this poet who declared that "they also serve who only stand and wait" in his poem "When I Consider How My Light Is Spent."
This pastoral elegy by John Milton is dedicated to Edward King. The title figure of this poem "knew himself to sing, and build the lofty rhyme."
Milton also wrote this epic, meant "to justify the ways of God to man." Satan declares, "Better to reign in Hell than serve in Heaven," in this work about the fall of Adam and Eve.

bonuses.leadin: This writer's pamphlet Areopagitica [air-ee-o-pah-JIT-ica] argues against censorship. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this French impressionist known for paintings of Racehorses at Longchamp and paintings of dancers, like Stage Rehearsal.
A miserable-looking woman stares abstractedly into space while a glass of the titular alcoholic beverage sits in front of her in this Degas painting.
Degas was friend and mentor to this painter of The Boating Party and many paintings of mother-and-child pairs, such as The Bath.

bonuses.leadin: This artist's aunt stands with her two children, next to her seated husband, with his back to the viewer in his The Belleli Family. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Beijing square tragically cleared on the night of June 4, 1989 after Deng Xiaoping's conservative faction used their control of the military.
Deng Xiaoping's conservatives thereby won their internal argument with Zhao Ziyang's liberal faction, a setback to Communist Party liberalization efforts in this country.
Tiananmen means "Heavenly Peace Gate", referring to a gate on the north of the square which is the main entrance to this ancient, restricted-access imperial residence of Chinese emperors.

bonuses.leadin: A protest here led to Jeff Widener's iconic photograph of a man, possibly named Wang Weilin, standing in front of four tanks. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this city, conquered by the Greeks with the aid of a large wooden horse.
According to Virgil, this king of Troy was killed by Neoptolemus during the fall of Troy. His children included Paris and Deiphobus.

This daughter of Priam was given the gift of prophecy by Apollo, but her prophecies were cursed to never be believed by anyone. Following the war, she was taken captive by Agamemnon, resulting in her death at the hands of Clytemnestra and Aegisthus.

bonuses.leadin: Neoptolemus threw the infant Astyanax off the walls of this city. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this 1701-1714 conflict, which began when Charles II left his throne to Philip V. Its battles included Blenheim and Malplaquet.
The War of the Spanish Succession was ended by this treaty, which was signed in the Netherlands in 1713 between Louis XIV and several other monarchs.
The two victorious commanders at Blenheim were an Austrian and British general. Name either.

bonuses.leadin: The North American theatre of this war was called Queen Anne's War. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this author of "Conjugal Lewdness, or Matrimonial Whoredom," who wrote a novel in which a trip to get a cargo of slaves goes awry, stranding Robinson Crusoe on an island.
The immoral title protagonist of this Defoe novel, written two years after the similar Moll Flanders, escapes from France to England and sleeps with her landlord and other nameless men.

This woman, Roxana's loyal maidservant, tests the intentions of a benefactor by seducing him and urges Roxana to accept the marriage proposal of a Dutch merchant, but is dismissed when she threatens Roxana's legitimate daughter.

bonuses.leadin: This author of "The True-Born Englishman" wrote an essay containing a dialogue between a bride-to-be and her friend, in which the former asks for "recipes" for contraception. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this foodstuff, which was presumably ground into flour and formed one half of Rome's "panem et circenses."
acceptableAnswers: obvious equivalents involving any plausible cereal

parts.text: Grain distribution usually centered on the temple to this earth goddess who was originally head of the Aventine Triad. She was the mother of Proserpina and identified by the Romans as the counterpart to Demeter.
Ceres was often depicted with this symbol of prosperity, which was created when an infant Zeus accidentally injured his nursemaid, the goat Amalthea ["am-uhl-THEE-uh"].

bonuses.leadin: The trade in this good, usually imported from North Africa, was represented in Roman times by the devotions of Cura Annonae. For 10 points each:

parts.text: The Golden Horde controlled the remnants of the Mongol Empire, which was founded by this original and greatest Khan who named Ogudei Khan his successor and led many Mongol raids.
This son of Jochi Khan ruled a major substituent of the Golden Horde, the Blue Horde. Along with his great general, Subotai, this man spurred the Mongol invasion of central Europe.
Batu and Subotai's conquest of this state culminated in the 1223 Battle of the Kalka River. This state's Golden Age occurred under the reigns of Vladimir the Great and Yaroslav the Wise.

bonuses.leadin: Name some things about the Golden Horde, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Give this surname. One person with this surname in "A Room of One's Own" is the real-life author of Romeo and Juliet; the other is his fictional sister, who dies in obscurity.
"A Room of One's Own" is by this author, who wrote about the Ramsay family's journey to the title building in her novel To the Lighthouse.
In this other work by Virginia Woolf, Septimus Smith commits suicide and the title woman laments her marriage to Richard while preparing for a dinner party.

bonuses.leadin: The feminist essay "A Room of One's Own" discusses the unequal opportunities of two people with this surname. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this chief god of the Greek pantheon.
Zeus's mother saved him from being eaten by this Titan, his crazy father. Zeus later overthrew him after forcing him to vomit out Poseidon and Hades.
Three of these figures had helped Cronus overthrow his father, Uranus. Their forge made Zeus' thunderbolts, helping to defeat the Titans.

bonuses.leadin: This deity fathered Persephone by Demeter, and Athena burst fully formed out of his head. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Prelude to a Broken Arm, which is a snow shovel with a painted-on dedication, and Fountain, which is a urinal signed "R. Mutt", are two of this Dadaist artist's "readymades".
A stuffed goat with an automobile tire ringing its torso is the most prominent feature of Monogram, one of the "combines" created by this proto-pop-artist.

Toy cars and an unrolled spring make up parts of Baboon and Young, a sculpture by this artist who also designed the huge unnamed steel sculpture in Chicago's Daley Plaza. He and George Braque coined the term collage.
acceptableAnswers: Pablo Diego José Francisco de Paula Juan Nepomuceno María de los Remedios Cipriano de la Santísima Trinidad Ruiz y Picasso

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about the use of found objects in art, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this collection of stories by Giovanni Boccaccio in which three young men and seven young women retreat to the countryside outside Florence and tell ten stories a night for ten days.

The young Florentines in The Decameron move to the country to avoid this catastrophic illness that swept across Europe in the 1340s and -50s, and which was nicknamed for the dark color of gangrenous skin in infected people.
Though Boccaccio is best-known for The Decameron, much of his career was devoted to writing these fourteen-line poems in the "Petrarchan" style.

bonuses.leadin: In this short story collection, Dioneo tells the story of "The Patient Griselda," and Fiametta tells the story of "Federigo's Falcon." For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this lake, the largest located entirely within Canada.
The Great Bear Lake is located southwest of Nunavut in this Canadian territory. Settlements here include Inuvik and Hay River.
This city located on the west side of its namesake river is the capital of the Northwest Territories.

bonuses.leadin: Uranium mining near this body of water has caused controversy and the town of Deline lies on its western shore. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with lung lobes and segments.
What is the main function of the bronchus in the respiratory system?
Name another component of the respiratory system related to lung lobes and segments.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human respiratory system.

parts.text: Name this fictitious force that causes objects to deflect perpendicular to their direction of motion. Hurricanes spin in opposite directions in different hemispheres due to this force.
The Coriolis force occurs in rotating reference frames, which belong to this class of reference frame. In general, these reference frames have nonzero acceleration.
The fact that, in many cases, the fourth and fifth of these points are stable is due to the Coriolis effect. These points are used in solutions to the three-body problem where one body is massless.

bonuses.leadin: A misconception is that this force dictates the direction water swirls when a toilet is flushed. For 10 points each:
